task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: counter strategy against a specific defense
methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict winning out of sample?
Are the suppression estimates and best/avoid recommendations reliable given sparse play-type exposure per defense?
Is adherence or the recommendation derived from outcomes (outcome-derived label, lookahead leakage)?
Is 54 series enough power for a series-level test, and can game-level units rescue it?
Do team quality, opponent strength, score state and garbage time confound any association?
evidence_establishes: Nothing: the retrieval returned no records, so no historical evidence was available for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether this question, or a close variant, has been tested before.
Whether adherence to a recommended mix predicted winning in any earlier analysis.
Which approaches failed, and why, in this project's earlier work.
Whether the suppression estimates are reliable enough to support recommendations.
own_inferences: The claim is vague. 'Suppression-conditional recommended mix' has no stated construction rule, so the test depends on how the recommendation is built and how adherence is scored.

If recommendations are fitted on the same games that are used to score adherence, adherence will partly encode the outcome (play-type points per possession feed both). That would produce a spurious positive association.
Points from a play type are part of scoring, and scoring drives winning, so a positive association is close to mechanical unless the recommendation is frozen using only prior data.
Team quality is a major confounder. Better teams run more efficient mixes and win more, so adherence may only proxy for quality.
Play-type exposure per defense is sparse (a handful of games per series), so the suppression estimates are noisy and the best/avoid labels are likely unstable.
With 54 series, only a large effect is detectable at the series level. A game-level design (a few hundred games) gives more power but needs clustering by series and by team.
Without a prior null or a validated construction, a naive test would more likely produce an artifact than a true positive.
uncertainties: The definition of suppression, of the recommended mix and of adherence is unspecified.
Which play types and how many categories are in the mix, which sets the multiplicity and the sparsity.
Whether 'predicts' means in-sample association or out-of-sample prediction.
Whether the 54 series include 2025-26 playoff series, which are only partial until 2026-06-21.
Quality of the derived play-type labels (initiator and play-type classification from play-by-play).
No prior-work record was available to calibrate the expected effect size.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so the decision rests only on the task statement and general methodological reasoning. The evidence neither supports nor discourages proceeding.

blocking_constraints.text: If the recommended mix or adherence is built from the same games' outcomes, the test is circular. The recommendation must be frozen from data strictly before each test game or series.
54 series gives low power for modest effects, and a recommendation built from earlier games leaves fewer usable test units.
The sparse per-defense play-type exposure makes suppression-conditional recommendations unstable.
Adherence is entangled with team quality and score state, so adjustment is required before any claim.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been studied. No claim is made about prior results.

risks.text: The recommended mix and adherence score may use outcome information (points per possession by play type), which makes adherence and winning mechanically linked.
Suppression estimates for a defense that use games including the test game or later games leak the future. Use only prior games (rolling or expanding-window).
Following high-efficiency play types raises points scored, and points scored determine the winner, so a positive association may be tautological.
54 series is small, and a series-level result is likely to be inconclusive unless the effect is large.
Few possessions per play type per defense make the suppression estimates noisy. Shrinkage is needed.
Adherence depends on the play-type classifier from play-by-play, and its reliability is unknown.
Team quality, opponent strength, home court, injuries, pace and garbage time confound the link between adherence and winning.
If the best/avoid labels are chosen from extreme noisy estimates, they regress toward the mean out of sample.
Many play types, thresholds and adherence definitions invite forking paths. Fix one primary specification in advance.
Defensive schemes and play-type rates change across seasons and within a series, so recommendations from earlier seasons may not transfer.
Without a placebo (adherence to a recommendation computed for a different defense), any effect cannot be attributed to the suppression-conditional part.

design.estimand: The incremental association between a game's adherence to a pre-registered recommended play-type mix for the specific opponent defense and the probability of winning that game. The reference model is the one with team strength, opponent strength and home court. The comparison is an adherence score built from the opponent-conditional recommendation versus one built from a league-average (non-conditional) recommendation. The quantity is the difference in out-of-sample log-loss or AUC and the adjusted log-odds coefficient for adherence.
design.unit: Primary: team-game (or game with both teams), clustered by series and team. Secondary: series-level, 54 series, as a descriptive check only.
design.sample: Games from 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, using only completed data. Recommendations for each defense are fitted only on that defense's games before the test game, or on prior seasons and earlier games, with shrinkage toward the league mean. Fix a minimum possession count per play type. Freeze the data cut and exclude 2025-26 playoff games until the data are complete (2026-06-21), or hold them as a final untouched test set. Exclude garbage-time possessions, defined in advance.
design.power: At 54 series the study is only powered for large effects; the sample is too small to detect a modest series-level effect, so the series-level result is not the primary test. The game-level sample is larger but clustered, so the effective sample is between the number of series and the number of games. Run a simulation-based power analysis before looking at outcomes, using the observed variation in adherence, a plausible odds ratio and clustering. Set a minimum detectable effect and declare the test inconclusive, not null, if the interval includes both zero and the minimum effect of interest.
design.controls: Pre-game team strength (rating from prior games only), opponent strength, home court, rest, pace, and possession-level score state (excluding garbage time). Include team and defense fixed or random effects. Shrinkage (empirical Bayes) for play-type suppression estimates. Check the play-type classifier on a hand-audited sample.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: adherence computed against a recommendation for a different, randomly assigned defense should have no incremental effect. (2) A permutation test that shuffles the recommended labels across defenses. (3) A time-reversed or lookahead version that is expected to show inflated results, as a leakage check. (4) Use a negative-control outcome such as first-quarter-independent or previous-game result. (5) Split-sample check: fit recommendations on seasons 2022-24 and test on 2024-26.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification and one primary adherence definition, registered before looking at outcomes. Secondary analyses (by season, by play type, regular season vs playoffs) are labelled exploratory and corrected with Holm or false discovery rate control.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the adherence coefficient from the opponent-conditional recommendation is positive with a 95% cluster-robust interval excluding zero, the out-of-sample log-loss improves over the strength-only and the league-average-recommendation baselines, and the placebo and permutation checks give null results. Rejected only if the interval excludes the pre-set minimum effect of interest. Otherwise report inconclusive. If a positive result disappears when the recommendation is frozen using prior data only, classify it as an artifact.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and derived play-type graph records as available on 2026-06-16. Hash and freeze the data and the code. Treat 2025-26 playoffs as incomplete until 2026-06-21 and add them only as a held-out confirmation after that date.
